subject: Question regarding the stan code generation logic

messages.author: 60f58ca1debdbe4d
messages.subject: Question regarding the stan code generation logic
parts:
I'm building a hierarchical model, and I was looking at the stan code generated by brms to understand how it works, and there is something I don't understand. So there is a parameter r_1 which is a matrix, that is later broken down to r_1_1 and r_1_2, like:

r_1_1 = r_1[, 1];  
r_1_2 = r_1[, 2]; 

and later in the model, we have:

eta[n] = eta[n] + r_1_1[J_1[n]] * Z_1_1[n] + r_1_2[J_1[n]] * Z_1_2[n]; 

why not just:

eta[n] = eta[n] + r_1[J_1[n], 1] * Z_1_1[n] + r_1[J_1[n], 2] * Z_1_2[n]; 

why are these two variable created, and then reported when they are the same are r_1?

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: Question regarding the stan code generation logic
parts:
There are two reasons for this at first glance strange code.

(a) It is sometimes faster. I am not fully sure about the cause, but I assume that repeatedly indexing elements of matrices (n times) is slower than extracting a column once and indexing a vector afterwards. At least I found examples, where it leads to 10-20% speed increase and never had an example where it was slower.

(b) It is easier to write Stan code for distributional models with group-level effects correlated across formulae. For instance, if you look at

data("sleepstudy", package = "lme4")
make_stancode(bf(Reaction ~ Days + (Days | ID | Subject),
                 sigma ~ Days + (Days | ID | Subject)),
                 sleepstudy)

you see that we can define more consistent parameter names.

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: Question regarding the stan code generation logic
parts:
When predicting the shape parameter (instead of assuming it to be constant across observations), we define a linear predictor for it.

The linear predictor might take on any real value while the shape must be postive and so we apply exp for being the inverse of the log link.
